sources.title: REST API for Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM
Tutorial: Create New Hires with HDL
Using the Oracle HCM Cloud Adapter with Oracle Integration 3

categories.name: REST framework essentials
categories.description: Headers, query parameters, paging and date-effective rules shared by every HCM REST resource.

items.name: Base URL, authentication and media types
items.summary: Every HCM REST call goes to /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/<resource> on your pod, authenticated as a service user with the right roles.
items.notes: Auth policy oracle/multi_token_over_ssl_rest_service_policy: Basic over SSL, SAML 2.0 bearer, JWT, or OAuth 2.0 (v1 resources need an OAuth token from OCI IAM). POST/PATCH body: Content-Type application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json; custom actions (terminate, uploadFile...): application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json. Accept application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json;q=0 returns only the status code (Supported_Media_Types). Oracle says: worker create/update can take several minutes (post-processing); use HDL for bulk loads, HCM Extracts for bulk extracts, Atom feeds (not REST polling) to detect changes. Do not send both a surrogate ID and its user key (e.g. AssignmentId and AssignmentNumber) in one payload.

items.name: Filtering with q and finder
items.summary: q filters a collection with SQL-like expressions (including child attributes); finder runs a predefined query with bind variables.
items.notes: q needs REST-Framework-Version 2 or higher. Operators: = > < >= <= <> in, is null, is not null, between, like, and, or, upper(). Only attributes marked queryable in /describe can be filtered; others return 400. Querying a child attribute returns the matching parents, but expand still returns the whole child array. URL-encode spaces/quotes in real calls. Finder syntax: ?finder=<name>;<var>=<value>,<var2>=<value2>.

examples.title: q examples
examples.code:
GET /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/workers?q=PersonNumber in (1053, 1200)
GET /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/workers?q=names.FirstName like '%Ki%'
GET /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/workers?q=(DateOfBirth > '1960-01-01') and (workRelationships.assignments.PositionId in (13,18))
GET /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/workers?finder=findByPersonId;PersonId=1564072335

items.name: fields, expand, onlyData, links
items.summary: Shape the response: pick attributes (fields), inline child resources (expand), drop link metadata (onlyData).
items.notes: Child fields use accessor:attr and ';' between accessors, nested accessors with dots (workRelationships.assignments). expand=all expands every level (heavy). If fields and expand are both sent, only fields is used. onlyData=true removes links and makes payloads much smaller for VBS/OIC.

items.name: Paging: limit, offset, hasMore, orderBy, totalResults
items.summary: Collections return one page at a time (default 25 items); loop with offset until hasMore is false.
items.notes: Response carries count, hasMore, limit, offset. orderBy=attr:asc,attr2:desc. totalResults=true adds an estimated row count (op-workers-get). The page does not state a maximum limit; test larger page sizes on your pod and prefer HCM Extracts for bulk.

items.name: REST-Framework-Version header
items.summary: Selects the ADF REST framework behaviour (1 to 8); each version is backward incompatible.
items.notes: v2: expanded q syntax. v3: nested children returned as collections (items/count/hasMore). v4: richer error payload (error code, o:errorPath). v5: typed custom-method results, some row LOVs become root LOVs. v6: @context object. v7: hides row-level LOVs. v8: CLOB as plain string, multi-select choice lists as arrays, encoded identifiers. Default may be 1 if not configured; GET the context root to see defaultFrameworkVersion and allowedFrameworkVersions. Oracle's HCM use-case examples send version 4.

items.name: Date-effective operations: effectiveDate and Effective-Of
items.summary: Read as of a date with ?effectiveDate=; create, update or delete date-effective rows with the Effective-Of header.
items.notes: Effective-Of: RangeMode=..;RangeStartDate=yyyy-MM-dd;RangeEndDate=..;RangeSpan=PHYSICAL_ROW_END_DATE|LOGICAL_ROW_END_DATE (+ RangeStartSequence/RangeEndSequence for multiple changes per day). PATCH modes: UPDATE (splits at range start, default start = context date), CORRECTION (overwrites record in context or exact physical range), END_DATE. DELETE modes: DELETE_CHANGES, ZAP. The op pages list more enum values (REPLACE_UPDATE, RECONCILE_CORRECTION...). Context date = effectiveDate on the GET (default sysdate). Never send EffectiveStartDate/EffectiveEndDate/EffectiveSequence/EffectiveLatestChange in the body. On POST, Effective-Of: RangeStartDate=<date> sets the start date (Create an Employee example).

examples.title: Date-effective assignment update from a date
Correction over an exact physical range

items.name: Batch requests (multiple parts in one call)
items.summary: ADF batch media type that groups several get/create/update/delete parts into one all-or-none request.
items.notes: The HCM guide lists media type application/vnd.oracle.adf.batch+json (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/farws/Supported_Media_Types.html) but has no batch page. Payload shape (parts[] with id, path, operation get|create|update|replace|delete, payload) and all-or-none behaviour were read in the Sales REST guide. POST target for HCM (version root /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/) is an assumption: test on a non-production pod first.

categories.name: Core HR and work structure REST
categories.description: Workers, employment (work relationships, assignments), documents and work structures (jobs, positions, grades, locations, departments).

items.name: Workers
items.summary: Main person + employment resource: create employees, contingent and pending workers, read and update person details.
items.notes: Finders: PrimaryKey(PersonId), findByPersonId(PersonId, SysEffectiveDate), findReports(AssignmentId, PersonNumber, DirectReportsFlag, ...). {workersUniqID} is the key in the item's self link, not PersonId text you build. Other child groups exist (passports, visa permits, driver licenses, photos, person DFF/EFF, external identifiers): confirm accessor names with /workers/describe. Supports effectiveDate and Effective-Of. Create/update are asynchronous-heavy; avoid for bulk. Replaces the older emps resource.

examples.title: Create an employee (trimmed from Oracle example)
Find by assignment number with children

items.name: Work relationships (and termination actions)
items.summary: Child of workers: one row per legal employer relationship (period of service); employment actions are custom actions here.
items.notes: Actions (POST .../action/<name>): terminate, reverseTermination, correctTermination, cancelWorkRelationship, changeLegalEmployer, changeStartDate, changePrimaryFlag, addTemporaryAssignment. Action bodies use lower camelCase keys and Content-Type application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json. Validate ActionCode/ReasonCode against actionsLOV and actionReasonsLOV first.

items.name: Assignments
items.summary: Child of a work relationship: job, department, position, grade, location, manager, status. Transfers, promotions and assignment changes are PATCH calls.
items.notes: Action endAssignment (POST .../action/endAssignment). Other subcategories: All Reports, Assignment EFF, legislative DFF, Grade Steps, Representatives, Work Measures (check accessor names in describe). Always PATCH with Effective-Of (UPDATE for a new dated change, CORRECTION to fix). Get ActionCode/ReasonCode from actionsLOV/actionReasonsLOV.

items.name: Public workers
items.summary: Read-only directory of active workers as of today with public information (no sensitive data).
items.notes: Subcategories: Assignments, Messages, Other Communication Accounts, Phones, Photos. Good for people pickers/org charts in VBS. Not for change detection (use Atom) or bulk (use HCM Extracts).

items.name: Actions and action reasons LOVs
items.summary: Look up valid ActionCode and ReasonCode values before hires, assignment changes and terminations.
items.notes: Reasons come from /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/actionReasonsLOV (Retrieve_Action_Reasons.html). Codes are configurable per customer: never hard-code without checking the target pod.

items.name: Document records
items.summary: Create, read, update and delete a person's documents of record (passport, visa, certificates) with attachments.
items.notes: attachments[].FileContents is Base64; response returns DatatypeCode FILE, DmDocumentId, FileUrl. Actions include findByAdvancedSearchQuery, downloadAttachments, generateDraftLetter and access checks. Other children: DFF/developer DFF, HR document types, banner override messages, candidate attachments. The document type must already exist.

items.name: Jobs
items.summary: Read job definitions as of a date.
items.notes: Finders: AltKey(EffectiveStartDate, JobCode, SetId), PrimaryKey(EffectiveEndDate, EffectiveStartDate, JobId), findByJobId(JobId, SysEffectiveDate). The 11.13.18.05 page lists only GET; load or change jobs with HDL Job.dat. Supports effectiveDate.

items.name: Positions
items.summary: Read positions as of a date (department, job, location, headcount, FTE, hiring status).
items.notes: Finders: AltKey(BusinessUnitId, EffectiveStartDate, PositionCode), PrimaryKey, findByPositionId(PositionId, SysEffectiveDate). Subcategories: DFF, EFF, legislative EFF, valid grades.

items.name: Grades
items.summary: Read grade name, code, type and grade steps.
items.notes: Subcategories: Grades DFF, Grades Steps. The steps accessor and GradeName/GradeCode come from Oracle's REST-Framework-Version example.

items.name: Locations V2
items.summary: Create, read, update and delete work locations (current date by default).
items.notes: Actions: changeEffectiveStartDate, splitLocationForChildUpdate, deleteLocationOtherAddresses, verifyForeignKeysOnDateChange. Subcategories: Addresses, Attachments, DFF, EFF container, legislative EFF. Oracle: create/update has post-processing and may take minutes; use HDL for bulk.

items.name: Departments (organizations)
items.summary: Read departments as of a date. The REST path is organizations, the doc group is called Departments.
items.notes: Subcategories: Organizations DFF, Organizations Extra Information. Only GET listed; load departments with HDL (Guidelines for Loading Organizations).

categories.name: Absence REST
categories.description: Recording absences and reading plan balances.

items.name: Absences
items.summary: Record, view, update and withdraw absences for a person, plus balance and plan-use actions.
items.notes: Attribute names are lower camelCase (unlike workers). Actions: getAbsenceTypeBalance, loadProjectedBalance, planUse, findByAdvancedSearchQuery, absenceDailyDetailsBreakdown, reprocessAbsencesAndRunPostApprovalProcess. Response source=REST, processingStatus, approvalStatusCd. Oracle shows no withdraw example: check allowed absenceStatusCd values via the AbsenceStatusVA LOV link in the response.

items.name: Plan balances
items.summary: Read accrual plan balances (including projected) for a person.
items.notes: Finder findByPersonIdPlanIdLevelDate:personId,planId,balanceAsOfDate (note ':' after the finder name in Oracle's example).

categories.name: Payroll and compensation REST
categories.description: Element entries, salaries and payroll relationships.

items.name: Element entries
items.summary: Create, read, update and delete payroll element entries (earnings, deductions, one-off bonuses).
items.notes: Finders: PrimaryKey(ElementEntryId, EffectiveStartDate, EffectiveEndDate), findByAssignmentNumber, findByElementEntryId, findByIntent. Amounts are updated on the elementEntryValues child (ScreenEntryValue), not on the entry. AssignmentId is not queryable; use AssignmentNumber or PersonNumber. DELETE with RangeMode=ZAP only for entries created in error.

examples.title: Correct an input value, then delete

items.name: Salaries
items.summary: Salary records for a worker's assignment: create, correct, delete, plus helper actions used by the Change Salary UI.
items.notes: Subcategories: Salary Components, Salary Rate Components, Salary Simple Components. Response adds SalaryFrequencyCode, DateTo, AdjustmentAmount, AdjustmentPercentage, ActionCode (e.g. CMP_CHANGE_SALARY). Many actions (getAssignmentInfo, coreHrSalaryRowValidation...) exist for UI flows. Get AssignmentId first from workers.

items.name: Payroll relationships
items.summary: Read a person's payroll relationship, payroll assignments and assigned payrolls.
items.notes: Finder findByAssignmentNumberPersonNumber shown in Oracle's query examples. Use case page: Manage_Payroll_Relationships.html. Confirm child names and update methods on the resource page before use.

categories.name: Talent and recruiting REST
categories.description: Recruiting candidates, job requisitions and performance goals.

items.name: Recruiting candidates
items.summary: Create, read, update and delete Recruiting Cloud candidates.
items.notes: Subcategories: address, attachments, citizenships, education, experience, languages, licenses and certifications, phone, skills, work preferences. Response returns CandidateNumber and CandidateType (e.g. ORA_EXTERNAL_CANDIDATE). PATCH example uses Content-Type application/vnd.oracle.adf.resourceitem+json.

items.name: Recruiting job requisitions
items.summary: Read job requisitions with state, phase, hiring manager, recruiter and location.
items.notes: Finders: PrimaryKey(RequisitionId), findByRequisitionNumber(RequisitionNumber). Only GET verified here; check the endpoint list for create/update before building writes.

items.name: Performance goals
items.summary: Read a worker's performance goals and their associated goal plans.
items.notes: Subcategory: Associated Goal Plans. Other goal resources exist (goalPlans with performanceGoals child and goalAssignActionBatch action, library goals, explore goals); check their pages before use.

categories.name: HCM Data Loader (HDL)
categories.description: Bulk load file format, SET instructions, key business-object files and REST automation of HDL.

items.name: HDL file format and keys
items.summary: Pipe-delimited .dat files (one per business object) zipped and loaded by HCM Data Loader; each component has a METADATA header and MERGE/DELETE data lines.
items.notes: Line instructions: METADATA, MERGE, DELETE, SET, COMMENT. Dates in Oracle examples are YYYY/MM/DD; open end date 4712/12/31. Keys: source keys (SourceSystemOwner + SourceSystemId) are recommended for create and update; reference parents with PersonId(SourceSystemId) etc. Register each owner as a code in lookup HRC_SOURCE_SYSTEM_OWNER (Manage Common Lookups). Best practices: one object type per zip for migration, load in dependency order, purge stage tables, always SET PURGE_FUTURE_CHANGES N for updates, never DELETE and MERGE the same record in one file. Check attribute names in View Business Objects.

items.name: HDL SET instructions
items.summary: Control lines at the top of a .dat file that change default load behaviour for that file.
items.notes: Must appear before the first METADATA line. Key ones: PURGE_FUTURE_CHANGES Y|N (default Y = replace; N = retain future-dated rows), INVOKE_POST_PROCESS Y|N, DISABLE_POST_PROCESS_TASKS RefreshManagerHierarchy|UpdatePersonSearchKeywords|FlattenPositionHierarchy, FILE_DELIMITER, FILE_ESCAPE, ENABLE_AUDIT_DATA, PURGE_AUDIT_DATA, CALCULATE_FTE, CREATE_DEFAULT_WORKING_HOUR_PATTERN, ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_LOAD_EVENTS (fire Atom feeds/events for HDL changes), EXTEND_DATA_SET_RETENTION (data sets otherwise deleted 30 days after last update).

examples.title: Typical update header
examples.code:
SET PURGE_FUTURE_CHANGES N
SET ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_LOAD_EVENTS Y
METADATA|Worker|SourceSystemOwner|SourceSystemId|...

items.name: Worker.dat: new hire
items.summary: Creates a person with name, legislative data, work relationship, work terms and assignment in one Worker.dat.
items.notes: Required for a hire: Worker, PersonName, WorkRelationship, WorkTerms, Assignment (PersonLegislativeData recommended). ActionCode HIRE on Worker, WorkTerms, Assignment. All component start dates must equal Worker StartDate / WorkRelationship DateStart. WorkTerms is a skeleton linking relationship to assignment; set job, grade, department on Assignment. PersonNumber optional when auto-generated (then source keys are mandatory). Email/phone/address components exist: confirm attribute names in View Business Objects (PersonPhone PhoneNumber must include legislation formatting, e.g. 555-0185).

examples.title: One hire (Oracle tutorial, one row per component)

items.name: Worker.dat: terminate, reverse, cancel
items.summary: Work relationship changes are loaded as flags on the WorkRelationship component.
items.notes: Terminate the work relationship, not the worker; assignments become inactive after the date and the supervisor relationship is end-dated. Reverse: ReverseTerminationFlag=Y. Correct date: new ActualTerminationDate + CorrectTerminationFlag=Y. Cancel: DELETE instruction with CancelWorkRelationshipFlag=Y. Change hire date: NewStartDate. One flag per record; flags not supported with full date-effective history loads.

items.name: Deleting worker components
items.summary: Rules for DELETE lines in Worker.dat: some components can be deleted, the whole worker cannot.
items.notes: Deletable: Person Address, Person Email, Person Phone (delete non-primary rows first or move primary), extra Person Legislative Data rows (one must remain), Assignment Grade Steps (not in same file when GradeId set to #NULL), Work Relationship (only with CancelWorkRelationshipFlag=Y). Not deletable: User Information, Person User Manual Roles (use the User object). Check per-component support in View Business Objects.

items.name: Salary.dat
items.summary: Loads salary rows (and optional components) for existing assignments.
items.notes: Oracle also documents user-key variants, updates, Delete a Salary, Purge Salaries for an Assignment, and pay rate / simple components (see fahbo TOC). HSDL cannot delete salaries.

items.name: ElementEntry.dat
items.summary: Bulk-loads recurring or non-recurring element entries and their input values.
items.notes: For a recurring entry with an end date, supply EffectiveEndDate on every line of that entry. MultipleEntryCount is not needed when source keys are used. Rollback: Import and Load Data > data set > Schedule Request > Roll Back, or (if loaded via the Initiate Data Loader payroll flow) Mark as Incomplete.

examples.title: Recurring entry, open end date (Oracle example)

items.name: PersonAbsenceEntry.dat
items.summary: Bulk-loads absence entries (e.g. migration or third-party absence systems).
items.notes: Employment must be valid at the start date; absence type must be valid and in the person's LDG; define the reason if the type requires one; assign a work schedule (else default schedule). Elapsed schedules need StartDateDuration/EndDateDuration (1 = full day, 0.5 = half day). Deleting a parent also deletes child rows (Guidelines for Loading Absence Entry).

examples.title: Time-based entry with user keys (Oracle example)

items.name: DocumentsOfRecord.dat
items.summary: Loads document records with file, URL or text attachments.
items.notes: DataTypeCode FILE, TEXT or WEB_PAGE. Attachment files go in the same zip under a folder named BlobFiles; File attribute = file name. Deleting the record deletes its attachments. An attachment can be overwritten only when the new file name is the same. Oracle's delete example key column is printed as 'DocumentdOfRecordId' (likely typo): confirm in View Business Objects.

examples.title: Passport with PDF (Oracle example)
examples.code:
METADATA|DocumentsOfRecord|PersonNumber|DocumentType|Country|DocumentCode|DocumentName|DocumentNumber|DateFrom|DateTo|IssuingCountryName
MERGE|DocumentsOfRecord|134003891|Passport|United Kingdom|PASSPORT_2442|UK Passport|355429|2012/04/03|2022/04/03|UK
METADATA|DocumentAttachment|PersonNumber|DocumentCode|DataTypeCode|URLorTextorFileName|Title|File
MERGE|DocumentAttachment|134003891|PASSPORT_2442|FILE|Passport_2442|JSmithPassport|JSmithPassport.pdf

zip layout: DocumentsOfRecord.dat + BlobFiles/JSmithPassport.pdf

items.name: SourceKey.dat
items.summary: Changes the source key (owner and ID) of an existing record, e.g. replace auto-generated FUSION keys with legacy IDs.
items.notes: Only for integration-enabled objects. BusinessObject and Component take the file discriminators (Worker, PersonAddress...).

items.name: HDL via REST: dataLoadDataSets
items.summary: Automate HDL: upload a zip to WebCenter Content, create the data set (import and load), poll status, submit load or rollback.
items.notes: Actions: /action/uploadFile (fileName, contentId, content Base64, fileEncryption NONE|PGPSIGNED|PGPUNSIGNED; small files only), /action/createFileDataSet (contentId, dataSetName, fileAction IMPORT_AND_LOAD|IMPORT_ONLY, thread and error % overrides), /{RequestId}/action/submit (fileAction LOAD|ROLLBACK, loadConcurrentThreads). Action bodies: Content-Type application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json; responses are {"result": {...}} (key names not documented: log the whole object). Roles: Use REST Service - Data Load Data Set (ORA_HRC_REST_SERVICE_ACCESS_DATA_LOAD_DATA_SETS), HRC_CREATE_FILE_DATA_SET_USING_REST_PRIV, HCM_DATALOADER_IMPORT_RWD for upload (https://docs.oracle.com/en/cloud/saas/human-resources/fahdl/overview-of-automating-data-loading.html). Manual path: File Import and Export (account hcm/dataloader/import) then Data Exchange > Import and Load Data.

examples.title: Upload, create data set, check status
examples.code:
POST /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/dataLoadDataSets/action/uploadFile
Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json

{ "fileName": "Worker.zip", "content": "<base64 zip>", "fileEncryption": "NONE" }

POST /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/dataLoadDataSets/action/createFileDataSet
Content-Type: application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json

{ "contentId": "<content id from result>", "dataSetName": "NEWHIRE_20261029", "fileAction": "IMPORT_AND_LOAD" }

GET /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/dataLoadDataSets/{RequestId}?expand=businessObjects,messages

categories.name: Fast Formula
categories.description: Syntax, arrays, contexts, functions, logging and two common formula types.

items.name: Formula structure and statements
items.summary: Statement order and core syntax of a Fast Formula: ALIAS, DEFAULT FOR, INPUTS ARE, assignments, IF/ELSE, WHILE, RETURN.
items.notes: Order: ALIAS, then DEFAULT, then INPUTS, then other statements. Give a DEFAULT for every database item that can be null and for inputs. You cannot assign to a database item. RETURN stops the formula; outputs must be listed in the RETURN that ends it. Create: search Fast Formulas in My Client Groups > Create > Formula Type + Effective Start Date > Continue > text > Compile > Save. Null checks with WAS DEFAULTED were not confirmed on the pages read this session: check the guide before relying on it.

examples.title: Oracle example: manager scheduled hours
examples.code:
/* DATABASE ITEM DEFAULTS BEGIN */
DEFAULT FOR per_asg_job_name IS ' '
/* DATABASE ITEM DEFAULTS END */
JOB_1 = PER_ASG_JOB_NAME
IF JOB_1 = 'Manager' then
(MIN_HOURS = 25
MAX_HOURS = 40
FREQUENCY = 'H')
else
(MIN_HOURS = 20
MAX_HOURS = 35
FREQUENCY = 'H')
return MIN_HOURS, MAX_HOURS, FREQUENCY

items.name: Arrays and array database items
items.summary: Typed arrays (DATA_INDEX) with FIRST/NEXT/EXISTS iteration; array DBIs are indexed from 1.
items.notes: Types: NUMBER_NUMBER, NUMBER_TEXT, DATE_NUMBER, DATE_TEXT, TEXT_NUMBER, TEXT_TEXT. Methods: A[i], .FIRST(def), .LAST(def), .EXISTS(i), .NEXT(i,def), .PRIOR(i,def), .COUNT, .DELETE(i), .DELETE(). Functions cannot take or return arrays; contexts cannot be arrays; reading a missing index raises an execution error. Array DBIs: DEFAULT_DATA_VALUE FOR <dbi> IS <value> at the top of the formula (database-items.html).

examples.title: Iterate an array (Oracle pattern)
examples.code:
NI = A.FIRST(-1234)
WHILE A.EXISTS(NI) LOOP
(
  VA = A[NI]
  NI = A.NEXT(NI, -1234)
)

items.name: Contexts, CHANGE_CONTEXTS and calling formulas
items.summary: Contexts (PERSON_ID, EFFECTIVE_DATE, HR_ASSIGNMENT_ID...) are bind values for DBIs; change them in a block, or call another formula.
items.notes: GET_CONTEXT(ctx, default) reads a context. CHANGE_CONTEXTS(ctx = expr, ...) ( ... ) applies only inside the block; prefer one block with several contexts over nesting. Formula calling formula: SET_INPUT('name', value), EXECUTE('FORMULA_NAME'), GET_OUTPUT('name', default), IS_EXECUTABLE('FORMULA_NAME') (formula-statements.html).

examples.title: Context change + call another formula
examples.code:
AREA1_VALUE = GET_CONTEXT(AREA1, ' ')
CHANGE_CONTEXTS(EFFECTIVE_DATE = '2026/01/01 00:00:00' (date))
(
  SET_INPUT('UNIT', 'Hourly')
  EXECUTE('RATE_FORMULA')
  HOURLY_RATE = GET_OUTPUT('RATE', 0.0)
)

items.name: Lookup functions: GET_VALUE_SET, GET_TABLE_VALUE
items.summary: Fetch data that has no database item: a table-validated value set, or a user-defined table cell.
items.notes: GET_VALUE_SET(value_set_code, bind) returns the first row's ID column (max 100 chars); value set must be Table validation, Character type, no aliases; binds passed as '|=PARAM=''value''' pairs. GET_VALUE_SET_ID is an alias. GET_TABLE_VALUE(table, column, row [,default or date]). Same page also lists GET_LOOKUP_MEANING, GET_MESG, GET_FND_MESG, GET_RATE, GET_VALUE_SET_VALUE(S), HR_TRACE, ESS_LOG_WRITE.

examples.title: Oracle examples
examples.code:
ASG_NUMBER = GET_VALUE_SET('SAMPLE_GET_ASG_NUM', '|=PERSON_ID=''' || POSITION3 || '''')
L_RATE = GET_TABLE_VALUE('WAGE RATES', 'Wage Rate', Rate_Code, 'DEFAULT')

items.name: Debugging and logging
items.summary: Write trace messages with ESS_LOG_WRITE (ESS process log) or HR_TRACE (PL/SQL trace), switched on by a debug flag.
items.notes: Logging slows processing: wrap it in a debug flag and recompile to enable (Improve Formula Performance). Troubleshoot: test seeded behaviour first, hard-code values, replace functions, then trace. Never delete and recreate a formula with the same name; edit it or create a new one. PAY_INTERNAL_LOG_WRITE was not found on the pages read: verify before use. Absence validation formulas can also return DEBUG_MESSAGE.

examples.title: Conditional logging
examples.code:
debug = 1
IF (debug = 1) THEN
(
  l_log = ESS_LOG_WRITE('FF debug start: hours=' || TO_CHAR(HOURS_WORKED))
)

items.name: Global Absence Entry Validation formula
items.summary: Validates an absence entry at submit time and blocks it with a custom error or warning.
items.path: Formula type: Global Absence Entry Validation
items.notes: Contexts include PERSON_ID, HR_ASSIGNMENT_ID, ABSENCE_TYPE_ID, ABSENCE_ENTRY_ID, LEGAL_EMPLOYER_ID, START_DATE, END_DATE, EFFECTIVE_DATE. Return VALID='N' plus ERROR_MESSAGE (text or a Manage Messages name), ERROR_CODE 'E' or 'W', TOKEN_NAME/TOKEN_VALUE arrays. DFF segments arrive as IV_ATTRIBUTE_ARR[1..30]: test with .EXISTS first.

examples.title: Minimal skeleton
examples.code:
DEFAULT FOR IV_START_DATE IS '4712/12/31 00:00:00' (date)
DEFAULT FOR IV_END_DATE IS '4712/12/31 00:00:00' (date)
INPUTS ARE IV_END_DATE (date), IV_START_DATE (date)
IF (DAYS_BETWEEN(IV_END_DATE, IV_START_DATE) + 1 > 10) THEN
(
  VALID = 'N'
  ERROR_MESSAGE = 'Absence cannot exceed 10 days'
  RETURN VALID, ERROR_MESSAGE
)
VALID = 'Y'
RETURN VALID

items.name: Element Input Validation formula
items.summary: Validates or defaults an element input value (or the whole entry) when entries are saved.
items.notes: Input-value level: input entry_value (declare correct type); return formula_status 'S' or 'E' (required) and formula_message. Element level can see PERSON_ID, HR_ASSIGNMENT_ID, PAYROLL_RELATIONSHIP_ID etc.; input-value level only LEGISLATIVE_DATA_GROUP_ID, DATE_EARNED, EFFECTIVE_DATE.

examples.title: Input value check
examples.code:
INPUTS ARE entry_value
IF (entry_value > 5000) THEN
(
  formula_status = 'E'
  formula_message = 'Amount above 5000 needs approval'
)
ELSE
(
  formula_status = 'S'
)
RETURN formula_status, formula_message

categories.name: HCM Extracts and Atom feeds
categories.description: Outbound bulk data (HCM Extracts, OIC pickup) and change events (Atom feeds).

items.name: HCM Extract definition and types
items.summary: Extract definition = data groups (root + connected children) > records > attributes; run through a payroll flow.
items.path: Data Exchange > HCM Extracts > Extract Definitions
items.notes: Define one root data group; data group connections build the hierarchy; one threading DBI per data group improves Changes Only runs. Avoid conditional actions and exclusion rules (slow, hard to debug); do it in BI Publisher templates instead. Extract types: Archive Retrieval, Benefit Carrier, Full Profile, HR Archive, Large Object, Recruiting Archive, Payroll Interface (auto-creates a changes-only parameter), Other Payroll Archive. Formula types: Extract Criteria, Extract Rule, Extract Advanced Condition, Extract Record (hcm-extract-formula-types.html). The UI path above is the usual one: confirm on your pod.

items.name: Extract delivery options
items.summary: Where and in what format extract output goes: Email, FTP, WebCenter Content, Data Loader Interface, Inbound Interface, Documents of Record, None.
items.notes: Output Data = XML (default), CSV needs no template; other formats need a BI Publisher report path + template. Integration Name (letters and digits only): UCM content ID = first 11 characters + extract process ID, used by OIC to find the file. FTP uses a File Transfer Configuration from the Data Exchange work area. Encryption needs PGP keys from Security Console. None delivery is for tests only.

examples.title: Content ID pattern
examples.code:
Integration Name: WORKERSYNC01
UCM content ID:   WORKERSYNC0<processId>   (first 11 chars + process ID)
Output Name:      Workers_%y%m%d_%H%M%S

items.name: OIC HCM Adapter: Extract Bulk Data
items.summary: Scheduled OIC integration that picks up the latest HCM Extract file from WebCenter Content and processes it in segments.
items.notes: Extract must use a WebCenter Content delivery option with a unique Integration Name, entered in the adapter field 'What is the Integration Name for HCM Extracts'. Keep a schedule parameter for the last processed Document ID (init 0), map it to lastProcessedDocumentID, read with Stage File 'Read File in Segments' using the extract schema exported from HCM, then store the new Document ID after the stage-file scope. The adapter also offers 'Import Bulk Data using HCM Data Loader (HDL)' > 'Submit an HCM Data Loader job' (import-bulk-data-hcm-data-loader-hdl.html).

items.name: Atom feeds: employee workspace
items.summary: Change-event feeds for new hires, person updates, assignment changes, terminations and more; Oracle's recommended way to detect changes.
items.notes: Only for employees, contingent and pending workers. newhire: hire, rehire, future hire. empupdate: name, work email, phone, address, personal, national ID, passport, citizenship, person DFF/EFF... empassignment: assignment, salary, manager, assignment DFF/EFF. Each entry has title, summary, published/updated dates, link /workers/<ID> (legacy /emps/<ID>) and JSON content with a Context array (PersonId, PersonNumber, PeriodOfServiceId, EffectiveDate, WorkerType, DMLOperation...). Workstructures and availability-pattern workspaces also exist. HDL changes fire feeds only with SET ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_LOAD_EVENTS Y. Roles needed for feeds were not confirmed in this session.

examples.title: Read new hires since a timestamp

items.name: Atom feeds: reading and polling
items.summary: Filter by updated or published time, page through results oldest first, and store the last processed timestamp.
items.notes: ISO 8601 timestamps (2017-07-14T14:04:00.000Z); min is exclusive, max inclusive. Use updated-min + orderBy=updated:asc to process future-dated events when they become effective; published-min + published:asc to process them immediately. archive=yes reads archived entries (Reading_a_Feed.html). Loop pages while a page is full; only advance the stored timestamp after an entry is processed successfully.

categories.name: BI Publisher / SQL tables
categories.description: Core HR tables for BI Publisher data models, read from Tables and Views for HCM.

items.name: PER_ALL_PEOPLE_F
items.summary: Core person row (global, non-legislative data), date-effective; holds PERSON_NUMBER.
items.notes: PK PER_PEOPLE_F_PK (PERSON_ID, EFFECTIVE_START_DATE, EFFECTIVE_END_DATE). START_DATE = earliest row's start (person creation). Always filter by an as-of date between the effective dates. Use in BI Publisher data models or OTBI direct SQL; there is no direct DB access in SaaS.

examples.title: Person as of a date
examples.code:
SELECT papf.person_id, papf.person_number, papf.start_date
FROM   per_all_people_f papf
WHERE  papf.person_number = :p_person_number
AND    :p_as_of BETWEEN papf.effective_start_date AND papf.effective_end_date

items.name: PER_PERSON_NAMES_F
items.summary: Date-effective person names (global and local name styles) with system-built display names.
items.notes: NAME_TYPE separates the global name from local names; filter NAME_TYPE = 'GLOBAL' (value used in Oracle's HDL example) to get one row per person.

examples.title: Global display name
examples.code:
SELECT ppnf.person_id, ppnf.display_name, ppnf.list_name
FROM   per_person_names_f ppnf
WHERE  ppnf.name_type = 'GLOBAL'
AND    :p_as_of BETWEEN ppnf.effective_start_date AND ppnf.effective_end_date

items.name: PER_PERIODS_OF_SERVICE
items.summary: Work relationships (one row per legal employer relationship); not date-effective.
items.notes: PERIOD_TYPE E (employee), C (contingent worker), N (non-worker). Matches REST workRelationships.PeriodOfServiceId. Index N3 on (PERSON_ID, PERIOD_TYPE, LEGAL_ENTITY_ID).

examples.title: Active workers on a date
examples.code:
SELECT papf.person_number, ppnf.display_name, ppos.date_start
FROM   per_all_people_f papf
JOIN   per_person_names_f ppnf ON ppnf.person_id = papf.person_id AND ppnf.name_type = 'GLOBAL'
       AND :p_as_of BETWEEN ppnf.effective_start_date AND ppnf.effective_end_date
JOIN   per_periods_of_service ppos ON ppos.person_id = papf.person_id
WHERE  :p_as_of BETWEEN papf.effective_start_date AND papf.effective_end_date
AND    ppos.date_start <= :p_as_of
AND    (ppos.actual_termination_date IS NULL OR ppos.actual_termination_date >= :p_as_of)

items.name: PER_ALL_ASSIGNMENTS_M
items.summary: Assignment and work terms rows; date-effective with multiple changes per day (sequence + latest-change flag).
items.notes: Table name confirmed in the Tables and Views for HCM (25A) contents under Global Human Resources, together with PER_ASSIGNMENT_SUPERVISORS_F, PER_EMAIL_ADDRESSES, PER_JOBS_F, HR_ALL_ORGANIZATION_UNITS_F and PER_LOCATION_DETAILS_F. Column names here mirror the REST attributes (AssignmentType, PrimaryFlag, EffectiveSequence, EffectiveLatestChange) and were NOT read on the table page: check the table page before use. Typical filters: ASSIGNMENT_TYPE (E/C/P vs work terms ET/CT/PT), PRIMARY_FLAG = 'Y', EFFECTIVE_LATEST_CHANGE = 'Y'.

examples.title: Primary assignment (verify columns first)
examples.code:
SELECT paam.person_id, paam.assignment_number, paam.job_id, paam.organization_id
FROM   per_all_assignments_m paam
WHERE  paam.assignment_type = 'E'
AND    paam.primary_flag = 'Y'
AND    paam.effective_latest_change = 'Y'
AND    :p_as_of BETWEEN paam.effective_start_date AND paam.effective_end_date

cookbook.title: New hire from an external system via OIC and HDL
cookbook.problem: An external ATS or HR system sends new hires; they must be created in Fusion HCM in bulk without manual entry.
prerequisites: Source system owner code (e.g. EXT_ATS) added to lookup HRC_SOURCE_SYSTEM_OWNER
Integration user with ORA_HRC_REST_SERVICE_ACCESS_DATA_LOAD_DATA_SETS, HRC_CREATE_FILE_DATA_SET_USING_REST_PRIV and HCM_DATALOADER_IMPORT_RWD
Valid legal employer, business unit, job codes and HIRE action on the target pod
OIC REST connection to https://{pod}.fa.{region}.oraclecloud.com with Basic or OAuth
steps: Map each source record to Worker.dat components: Worker, PersonName, PersonLegislativeData, WorkRelationship, WorkTerms, Assignment. Use SourceSystemId = external employee ID with suffixes (_NME, _POS, _TRM, _ASG) and the same start date on every component.
In OIC, build the .dat text (stage file write), zip it as Worker.zip and Base64-encode it.
POST /dataLoadDataSets/action/uploadFile with fileName and content; log the whole result object and read the content ID.
POST /dataLoadDataSets/action/createFileDataSet with contentId, dataSetName and fileAction IMPORT_AND_LOAD; read the request ID from result.
Poll GET /dataLoadDataSets/{RequestId} (wait loop, e.g. every 60 s) until DataSetStatusMeaning shows completion; then read ObjectSuccessCount and ObjectLoadErrorCount.
On errors, GET ?expand=messages and send MessageText with SourceSystemId back to the source system or a support mailbox.
testing: Load 1-2 hires on a test pod first and check ObjectSuccessCount
GET /workers?q=PersonNumber='<new number>'&expand=workRelationships.assignments to confirm assignment, BU and job
Load the same file again: source keys should update, not duplicate
rollback: Data set rollback: POST /dataLoadDataSets/{RequestId}/action/submit with fileAction ROLLBACK (only for objects that support rollback; confirm for Worker)
For a wrong hire: cancel the work relationship (REST action cancelWorkRelationship or HDL DELETE WorkRelationship with CancelWorkRelationshipFlag=Y)
Fix data and reload using the same source keys

cookbook.title: Incremental worker sync with Atom feeds
cookbook.problem: A downstream system (AD, badge, LMS) needs new hires, changes and terminations without full daily extracts.
prerequisites: Integration user that can read Atom feeds and workers REST (confirm roles in the security guide)
A store for the last processed timestamp per feed (OIC lookup, DB table, or schedule parameter)
Decision: process future-dated events when effective (updated) or immediately (published)
steps: For each collection (newhire, empupdate, empassignment, termination), GET /hcmRestApi/atomservlet/employee/<collection>?updated-min=<last>&page-size=25&page=1&orderBy=updated:asc.
For each entry, parse the JSON Context (PersonId, PersonNumber, EffectiveDate, DMLOperation) and the /workers link.
Fetch current details only for that person: GET /workers?q=PersonId=<id>&fields=...&onlyData=true&effectiveDate=<EffectiveDate>.
Upsert into the target system keyed on PersonNumber; on success save entry.updated as the new last processed timestamp.
Continue to the next page while a page is full; stop the run on the first failure so nothing is skipped.
If HDL loads must also be synced, include SET ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_LOAD_EVENTS Y in those HDL files.
testing: Hire a test person and update their phone, then confirm entries appear in newhire and empupdate
Re-run with the same timestamp: upserts must be idempotent
Check the min boundary: updated-min is exclusive
rollback: Nothing changes in HCM; to reprocess, reset the stored timestamp to an earlier value
Disable the schedule if the target system receives bad data

cookbook.title: Create and reschedule an absence via REST
cookbook.problem: A custom VBS page or chatbot must submit leave for an employee and show the balance.
prerequisites: Absence type code, employer (legal employer name) and person number valid on the start date
User with absence REST access for that person
Work schedule assigned to the worker
steps: Optional: read the balance with GET /planBalances?finder=findByPersonIdPlanIdLevelDate:personId=..,planId=..,balanceAsOfDate=..
POST /absences with personNumber, employer, absenceType, startDate/startTime, endDate/endTime, absenceStatusCd SUBMITTED.
Store personAbsenceEntryId from the response and show approvalStatusCd and duration to the user.
To change dates, PATCH /absences/{personAbsenceEntryId} with new startDate/endDate.
Add validation rules with a Global Absence Entry Validation fast formula instead of client-side checks.
testing: GET /absences/{personAbsenceEntryId} and compare duration, approvalStatusCd and processingStatus
Check the entry in the employee's absence UI
Try an invalid absence type and confirm a 400 with a readable message (use REST-Framework-Version 4)
rollback: DELETE /absences/{absencesUniqID} for an entry created in error
Or PATCH the dates back; check AbsenceStatusVA LOV for withdraw status values before using one

cookbook.title: Bulk element entries via HDL with rollback
cookbook.problem: Load a one-time allowance or bonus for many workers before a payroll run, with a safe undo.
prerequisites: Element, input value names and LDG name confirmed
Assignment source keys (or user keys) for each worker
Payroll not yet run for the period
steps: Build ElementEntry.dat with ElementEntry and ElementEntryValue lines; use source keys like <assignment>_<element>_<period>.
For an end-dated recurring entry, put EffectiveEndDate on every line of that entry.
Zip and upload via File Import and Export (account hcm/dataloader/import) or dataLoadDataSets uploadFile, then Import and Load Data (or createFileDataSet).
Review the data set: Total Objects, errors and failed lines; fix and reload only failed lines.
Spot-check entries with GET /elementEntries?q=PersonNumber='<n>' before the payroll run.
testing: Count of loaded objects equals file rows
GET one entry with expand=elementEntryValues and check ScreenEntryValue
Run a QuickPay or test payroll for one worker
rollback: Data Exchange > Import and Load Data > select data set > Total Objects > Schedule Request > Action Roll Back > Submit
If loaded with the Initiate Data Loader payroll flow: Payroll Flow page > Actions > Mark as Incomplete > Continue

cookbook.title: HCM Extract delivered to OIC, then to SFTP
cookbook.problem: A vendor needs a daily worker file; the extract should be produced in HCM and moved by OIC.
prerequisites: Extract definition with the required data groups and attributes
Delivery option of type WebCenter Content with a unique Integration Name
Extract schema exported from HCM
OIC HCM Cloud Adapter connection and an FTP/SFTP connection (assumed adapter choice)
steps: Create the extract (root data group, records, attributes); output CSV or Data (XML); schedule its payroll flow.
Set delivery type WebCenter Content and Integration Name (letters/digits; first 11 chars + process ID become the UCM content ID).
In OIC create a scheduled integration with a schedule parameter for the last processed Document ID, initial value 0.
Invoke the HCM Cloud Adapter extract bulk data operation; map the parameter to lastProcessedDocumentID.
Use Stage File 'Read File in Segments' on the returned file name and directory, with the exported extract schema; inside the scope transform and write to SFTP.
After the stage-file scope assign the new Document ID to the schedule parameter.

examples.title: Adapter field
examples.code: What is the Integration Name for HCM Extracts: WORKERSYNC01

testing: Run the extract once and confirm a file with content ID WORKERSYNC0<processId> exists
Run the integration twice: second run must not resend the same document
Validate row counts against a BI report
rollback: Disable the delivery option (Enabled) or the OIC schedule
Reset the schedule parameter to an older Document ID to resend a file

cookbook.title: Read worker and assignments for a VBS page
cookbook.problem: A Redwood/VBS page must show a worker's name, legal employer and assignments quickly.
prerequisites: VBS service connection to HCM REST workers (Create a Service Connection from a Service Specification)
Signed-in user with access to the person (REST data security applies)
steps: Create a service connection for /hcmRestApi/resources/11.13.18.05/workers and add header REST-Framework-Version: 4.
Call GET workers with q on PersonNumber, fields for only the attributes you show, and onlyData=true.
Pass effectiveDate when the page has an as-of date picker.
Flatten workRelationships.items[].assignments.items[] in a page module function for a table.
Use publicWorkers for people pickers that need only public data.

examples.title: Page module flatten function

testing: Test the endpoint in the service connection Test tab with a known PersonNumber
Compare with the same GET in Postman as the same user
Check page with a user lacking access: expect empty items, not an error
rollback: Read-only; revert the extension to the previous published version if needed

cookbook.title: Terminate a worker via REST (HDL alternative)
cookbook.problem: An offboarding workflow must terminate a work relationship on a given date with a valid action.
prerequisites: Valid termination ActionCode/ReasonCode (actionsLOV, actionReasonsLOV)
workersUniqID and PeriodOfServiceId of the relationship
User with terminate access
steps: GET /actionsLOV?q=ActionName like '%Termination%' to confirm the action code.
GET /workers?q=PersonNumber='<n>'&expand=workRelationships and take the worker self link and PeriodOfServiceId.
POST .../workRelationships/{PeriodOfServiceId}/action/terminate with actionCode and terminationDate (Content-Type application/vnd.oracle.adf.action+json).
Bulk alternative: Worker.dat WorkRelationship with TerminateWorkRelationshipFlag=Y, ActualTerminationDate, ActionCode, ReasonCode and SET PURGE_FUTURE_CHANGES N.
Downstream systems pick the change from the termination Atom feed.
testing: Response {"result": "true"}
GET the work relationship: TerminationDate is set
After the date, assignment status is inactive
rollback: REST action reverseTermination (or correctTermination to change the date) on the same work relationship; check the action page for its body

cookbook.title: Upload a document of record with attachment
cookbook.problem: Scanned documents (passport, visa, certificate) from a portal must be stored on the employee's document records.
prerequisites: Document type exists and allows the attributes you send
Person number of the employee
File Base64-encoded (REST) or placed in BlobFiles (HDL)
steps: POST /documentRecords with PersonNumber, DocumentType, DocumentCode, DocumentName and attachments[{FileName, FileContents}].
Store DocumentsOfRecordId from the response.
For many files use DocumentsOfRecord.dat with DocumentAttachment lines and the files in BlobFiles/ in the same zip.
To replace a file via HDL, reload with the same attachment file name.
testing: GET /documentRecords/{DocumentsOfRecordId}?expand=attachments shows UploadedFileName and FileUrl
Open the record in the UI and download the file
rollback: DELETE /documentRecords/{DocumentsOfRecordId} (attachments are deleted with the record)
HDL DELETE line for DocumentsOfRecord (confirm key attribute name in View Business Objects)
